subject: CORMORANT-4B runtime ABI & tokenizer parity check — onboarding gating question
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Omar Alvarez <omar@acme-ai.com>
Cc: ACME AI SRE <sre@acme-ai.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: CORMORANT-4B runtime ABI & tokenizer parity check — onboarding gating question

Hi all,

Quick cross-functional flag on the CORMORANT-4B intake from Acme. During the preflight scans Marcus ran, the tokenization histogram for the supplied vocab differs from the tokenizer we have in the staging runtime (prefix byte-ordering + an extra BOS token). That mismatch shows up as shifted KV cache indices on a quick local run: responses are coherent but certain long-context scenarios return garbled sections.

Irene — from runtime POV, is this something we can safely canonicalize at the adapter layer (translate token ids at request ingress) or is the ABI/layout difference too risky for a warm KV cache across variants?

Karthik / Laura — product asks: Acme needs an onboarding date for next-week beta. We should decide whether to pin the serving variant to Acme's published weights (v1.2) or onboard with a translation shim and mark as experimental. If we pin we should define TTL for pin and telemetry to capture regression.

Omar / SRE — can you confirm the tokenizer artifact you supplied (cormorant-tokenizer-v1.2.zip) and whether there's a compat build that matches Redwood's runtimes?

Attached: tokenizer-parity-checklist.xlsx (Marcus), small ABI diff Marcus captured (cormorant-4b-abi-diff.patch), and a proposed canary-runbook draft.

Proposed next steps:
- Quick decision today on provisional pin vs adapter shim
- If pin: set pin window (2 weeks) + canary in us-west-2 with telemetry flag INF-4721
- If shim: schedule a 2-day engineering slot to harden translation layer and thorough QA

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Omar Alvarez <omar@acme-ai.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CORMORANT-4B runtime ABI & tokenizer parity check — onboarding gating question

Thanks for the heads up, Soojin. Reading Marcus's patches and the tokenizer checklist: the issue is two-fold.

1) Token mapping: Acme's tokenizer reserves token_id 1 for <BOS>. Our runtime uses token_id 1 for a soft-prefix sentinel. That alone can be handled with a per-model id-map at ingest (cheap, reversible).
2) Weirder: the weight serialization layout in v1.2 places attention KV blocks with little-endian chunking that differs from our quantized loader's expectation. That causes cache index misalignment when we restore a snapshot across warm sessions — we're seeing off-by-8 token shifts in the replayed KV stream.

My recommendation: temporary variant pin to cormorant-4b@v1.2 on Redwood's production pool, while we do a short engineering run to add a reversible translation for the KV layout or extend the loader to detect layout via a header flag. Pin window: 14 days. Canary: 1% traffic in us-west-2, controlled by feature flag (INF-4721). Telemetry: add a regression metric for "kv_index_shift" and a user-facing quality metric for long-context perplexity.

If Acme can publish a build that uses our standard serialization (little/big endian normalized) that shortens the work. Otherwise we'll proceed with pin + fix.

I'll own the loader change estimate: ~2.5 engineer-days (I can scope more precisely if we decide shim vs loader).

- Irene

Subject: Re: CORMORANT-4B runtime ABI & tokenizer parity check — onboarding gating question

Adding a couple of test notes from the artifact runs I did:
- The tokenizer-parity-checklist.xlsx has a reproducible test case (attached) — comparing model output for a 4k prompt with and without the id-map shows the garbled spans from token 1824 onward.
- The cormorant-4b-abi-diff.patch contains a short header sniff that detects the layout, but its not safe to rely on in prod without a fallback.

If we pin, we should also disable cross-region warm cache transfers for that variant during the pin window; that avoids mismatches when cache snapshots are transported. The canary-runbook.md includes the toggle.

Also: We should notify Support and CSM that short-term we will have a 'locked' variant for Acme so they don't try to change model-weight parameters mid-pin.

Marcus

Date: 2026-10-03T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CORMORANT-4B runtime ABI & tokenizer parity check — onboarding gating question

Appreciate the quick triage. We ran an internal reproducer and can confirm token_id mapping mismatch and a difference in the little-endian chunking for attention blocks in our current v1.2 artifact.

Two options on our side:
- We can publish a v1.2.1 weights bundle that adopts Redwood's serialization header (low friction) — ETA 48 hours, but it requires a new signed artifact and a quick security stamp.
- Or we proceed with your pin + loader shim; that buys us time while we formalize the new release.

If you pick the pin path, please share the canary runbook and the telemetry hooks so we can add our own instrumentation on the Acme side to validate that output quality matches their expectations.

Thanks,
Omar
Acme AI — Model Ops

Decision summary and action items (agreed):

1) Provisional decision: Pin the production serving variant to cormorant-4b@v1.2 for a 14-day window starting 2026-10-05.
   - Purpose: avoid incorrect KV cache restore across warm sessions while we either ingest a new Acme artifact or implement a loader shim.
2) Canary: 1% traffic in us-west-2 controlled by feature flag INF-4721. Marcus to flip cross-region warm cache transfer off for this variant during the pin.
3) Engineering work: Irene to scope and own the loader shim (2.5 engineer-days estimate). If Acme publishes v1.2.1 within 48 hours, we fast-track replacement and close the pin early.
4) Telemetry: add kv_index_shift metric + long-context perplexity delta. Laura to add ticket to dashboards and coordinate with Support + CSM.
5) Communication: Soojin will notify CSM and Support; Omar will coordinate on a signed v1.2.1 artifact if available.

Attachments: canary-runbook.md (Marcus updated), tokenizer-parity-checklist.xlsx (Marcus), cormorant-4b-abi-diff.patch (Marcus).

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync for Monday 10/05 to validate canary gating and the switch plan. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround.

Soojin
